<!-- file: docs/tasks/backup-and-monitoring.md -->

# Back up, restore and monitor Siphon

**Goal:**
- a backup you can restore on the same host or a new one;
- numbers Prometheus can alert on;
- a choice of how long Siphon keeps its history.

All three are operator settings. You run them on the host, or set them in
`siphon.yaml`. None of them can be changed from the portal or the API.

## What a backup contains

Everything users built lives next to `server.db` (`/var/lib/siphon` with the
NixOS module and in the OCI image):

| In the archive | What |
|---|---|
| `state.db` | tasks and every config revision, jobs, approvals, the audit log, notifications |
| `secrets/` | the secret values pasted in the portal or passed with `--secret` |
| `credentials/` | subscription logins (`siphon connect login`, `credentials import`) |

**Not included:** `siphon.yaml` and `server.token`. Keep those with your own
config management (Nix, /etc, your secrets tool).

**Treat the archive like the secrets themselves.** It holds every token
Siphon was given. Siphon creates it readable only by its owner (mode 0600). Keep it that way, or encrypt it.

## Back up

```sh
siphon backup create -db /var/lib/siphon/state.db /backups/siphon.tar.gz
# backed up to /backups/siphon.tar.gz (1843200 bytes, 4 secrets, 1 logins)
```

- **Siphon keeps running.** The database copy is consistent (SQLite's
  `VACUUM INTO`), even while jobs are being written.
- **Who runs it:** the user that owns the state. That's `siphon` on NixOS:
  `sudo -u siphon siphon backup create …`.
- **`-db` or `-config`:** `-db` points straight at the database. Or give
  `-config siphon.yaml` and the `server.db` in it is used.
- **Existing file:** an existing file is refused unless `--force` is given.

**Encrypted, or straight into a backup tool:** use `-` to write to stdout.
Stdout is refused when it's a terminal.

```sh
sudo -u siphon siphon backup create -db /var/lib/siphon/state.db - | age -r age1… > siphon.tar.gz.age
sudo -u siphon siphon backup create -db /var/lib/siphon/state.db - | restic backup --stdin --stdin-filename siphon.tar.gz
```

**OCI image:**

```sh
podman exec siphon siphon backup create -db /var/lib/siphon/state.db - > siphon.tar.gz
```

### Every day, on NixOS

```nix
services.siphon.backup = {
  enable = true;
  dir = "/var/backup/siphon";   # default
  calendar = "daily";           # systemd OnCalendar
  keep = 7;                     # newest archives kept
};
```

This adds `siphon-backup.timer`, which writes
`siphon-<UTC time>.tar.gz` into `dir` (mode 0700, owned by `siphon`) and
deletes all but the newest `keep`. Run one now with
`systemctl start siphon-backup`. Point your offsite backup at `dir`.
A failed run shows as a failed `siphon-backup.service`. To hear about it,
add `systemd.services.siphon-backup.unitConfig.OnFailure` pointing at your
alerting unit (the `service-failed` template does this through Siphon).

## Restore

Restore works only with Siphon **stopped**, because it replaces the database
underneath it.

```sh
systemctl stop siphon
sudo -u siphon siphon backup restore -db /var/lib/siphon/state.db /backups/siphon.tar.gz
# restore replaces existing state: db 1843200 bytes, 212 jobs, 4 secret files, 1 credential files
# continue? [y/N] y
# restored; the previous state is in /var/lib/siphon/pre-restore-20261008T201500Z; start siphon, then run siphon validate
systemctl start siphon
siphon validate -config /etc/siphon/siphon.yaml
```

- **Checked first:** before anything is changed, the whole archive is
  checked: its names, its size (1 GiB at most), its version and the
  database's integrity. A bad archive is refused and nothing is touched.
- **Nothing is deleted:** the current state is moved into
  `pre-restore-<time>/`. Delete it once you're happy.
- **Refusals:**
  - **While Siphon is running:** exit 5.
  - **As the wrong user** (root on NixOS, for example): refused with the
    user to use.
  - **A backup from a newer Siphon:** refused. Upgrade first.
- **Only restore archives you made.** An archive holds tasks, commands
  and secrets, so restoring one is the same as being allowed to change
  Siphon's config. Siphon checks that it's a Siphon database (its schema, and
  that it has no triggers or views), but it can't tell your tasks from
  someone else's.
- **Older backups** are fine. Siphon updates the database when it starts.
- **From stdin** (`… | siphon backup restore … -`): pass `--yes`, because
  stdin can't also answer the question. Without a terminal, `--yes` is
  always needed when state exists.

### Move to a new host

1. On the new host, install Siphon with the same `siphon.yaml` (and the same
   files that its `file:` and `env:` references point to). Don't start it, or
   stop it again.
2. Copy the archive over and restore it as above. The state directory is
   created if it's missing.
3. Start Siphon and run `siphon validate`. Webhook URLs change if the host
   name does: update `server.public_url` and each service's webhook setting.

## Metrics

`GET /metrics` serves the Prometheus text format. It needs a token, so
nothing is open without it. A wrong token gets 401, and repeated failures get
429.

**Give Prometheus a scrape token.** It opens `/metrics` and nothing else:
the API and the portal refuse it. Make one with at least 32 characters,
different from `server.token` (`openssl rand -hex 32`):

```yaml
# siphon.yaml
server:
  metrics:
    token: file:/etc/siphon/metrics-token
```

On NixOS, pass the file like the login token:

```nix
services.siphon.credentials.metrics-token = "/run/agenix/siphon-metrics-token";
services.siphon.settings.server.metrics.token = "file:/run/credentials/siphon.service/metrics-token";
```

Then point Prometheus at the same value:

```yaml
# prometheus.yml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: siphon
    scrape_interval: 30s
    static_configs: [{ targets: ["siphon.lan:8080"] }]
    authorization:
      credentials_file: /run/secrets/siphon-metrics-token
```

| Metric | Labels | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `siphon_build_info` | `version` | always 1 |
| `siphon_jobs` | `state` | jobs Siphon holds, by state (finished ones for the retention period) |
| `siphon_jobs_finished_last_hour` | `state` | done, failed, cancelled in the last hour |
| `siphon_queue_oldest_seconds` | | age of the oldest queued job (0: none) |
| `siphon_approvals_pending` | | jobs waiting for approval |
| `siphon_approval_oldest_seconds` | | how long the oldest one has waited (0: none) |
| `siphon_agent_runs_today` | | agent runs in the last 24 h |
| `siphon_agent_runs_daily_limit` | | `limits.agent_runs_per_day` |
| `siphon_source_failing` | `source` | 1 while a polled source keeps failing |
| `siphon_source_last_poll_timestamp_seconds` | `source` | when it was last polled |
| `siphon_rule_error` | `rule` | 1 when a rule has an error (see `siphon why`) |
| `siphon_notifications` | `channel`, `state` | notification deliveries by state (`pending` = retrying) |

- **Use the scrape token, not the login token.** The login token
  (`server.token`) also works on `/metrics`, so older scrape configs keep
  working. But it gives whoever reads the scrape config the whole API. Either
  way, keep the token in a file only Prometheus can read
  (`credentials_file`), not inline in `prometheus.yml`.
- **A changed token needs a restart** of Siphon, like `server.token`.
- **Labels** are only names from your config. Metrics never include job
  contents, errors, URLs or secrets.
- **Computed per scrape:** every value is read from the database when
  Prometheus asks, so restarts don't reset anything.

### Example alerts

```yaml
groups:
  - name: siphon
    rules:
      - alert: SiphonJobFailed
        expr: siphon_jobs_finished_last_hour{state="failed"} > 0
      - alert: SiphonApprovalWaiting
        expr: siphon_approval_oldest_seconds > 72000      # 20 h of the 24 h
      - alert: SiphonSourceFailing
        expr: siphon_source_failing == 1
        for: 15m
      - alert: SiphonNotificationsStuck
        expr: siphon_notifications{state="pending"} > 0
        for: 30m
      - alert: SiphonAgentCapNear
        expr: siphon_agent_runs_today >= 0.9 * siphon_agent_runs_daily_limit
```

[Notifications](notifications.md) already message a person about single
events. Metrics are for dashboards and for alerting through what you
already run.

## How long history is kept

```yaml
# siphon.yaml
server:
  retention:
    jobs: 2160h         # finished jobs with their approvals and notifications (default 720h = 30 days)
    audit: 8760h        # the audit log (default 720h)
    seen_events: 168h   # ids used to drop duplicate webhook deliveries (default 168h = 7 days)
```

- **Units:** values are durations in hours (`h`). Unset or `0` keeps the
  default.
- **Minimum:** each value must be at least `24h`.
- **When it runs:** cleanup runs once a day, so a change applies at the next
  run.
- **Keep the audit log at least as long as you need to answer "who approved
  that?"**


---

<!-- file: docs/tasks/notifications.md -->

# Get told when something needs you

**Goal:** a message on your phone or in Slack when:
- an agent run waits for your approval;
- a job fails;
- a polled source keeps failing.

Without this, nothing tells you. Approvals sit until they expire.

## ntfy (your phone)

Install the ntfy app and subscribe to a topic with a long, unguessable name.
The topic name is the secret, so Siphon stores the URL write-only:

```sh
printf %s https://ntfy.sh/siphon-k3v9q2x7p | siphon notify add phone --type ntfy --url - --yes
siphon notify test phone        # → sent (HTTP 200), and your phone buzzes
```

A protected topic on your own ntfy server needs an access token:

```sh
siphon notify add phone --type ntfy --url @ntfy-url.txt --token @ntfy-token.txt --yes
```

## Slack

Create an **incoming webhook** for a channel (Slack: *Apps → Incoming
Webhooks*), then:

```sh
siphon notify add team --type slack --url @slack-hook.txt --events approval,reminder,failed --yes
siphon notify test team
```

## A webhook (anything else)

Siphon POSTs JSON to any https URL. You can add a bearer token
(`--token`).

```sh
siphon notify add relay --type webhook --url @relay-url.txt --token @relay-token.txt --yes
```

```json
{"event": "approval", "rule": "pr-review", "job": 42, "source": "",
 "title": "Approval needed: pr-review (job 42)",
 "message": "agent run waits for approval; expires in 24h",
 "url": "https://siphon.example.com/jobs/42", "at": "2026-10-08T14:02:11Z"}
```

`event` is one of `approval`, `reminder`, `failed`, `source`, `source_ok`
or `test`. `job` is `0`, and `rule` is empty, for source messages.

## What sends a message

| `--events` | When | Sent |
|---|---|---|
| `approval` | a job starts waiting for approval (including each routine step that asks) | once per wait |
| `reminder` | an approval has 4 h or less left (of 24 h) | once per wait |
| `failed` | a job ends `failed`: it errored, was interrupted too often, or its approval expired | once per job |
| `source` | a polled source has failed for 15 minutes; then once more when it recovers | once per outage |

Leave out `--events` to get all four.

**A new channel only hears about new things.** It sends nothing from
before you added it, apart from the last half-minute or so.

## What a message contains

- **Included:** the rule, the job number, the kind of action, the source
  and the time left.
- **Never included:** the event, the prompt, the job's output, or any
  secret. Those can be sensitive, and the message goes to an outside
  service.
- **Link:** set `server.public_url` in `siphon.yaml` and each message links
  to the job in the portal. Without it, the message says which command to
  run (`siphon approve 42`).

No message can approve a job by itself. You approve in the portal or with
the CLI, logged in.

## Verify

- **Portal:** **Notifications** lists each channel with its last delivery,
  a **Test** button, and the recent deliveries. A job's page shows what was
  sent about it.
- **CLI:**
  ```sh
  siphon notify log                  # recent deliveries: sent, pending (retrying), failed, suppressed
  siphon notify log --job 42
  siphon get notify                  # the channels (url and token shown masked)
  siphon delete notify phone
  ```

## Limits

- **Retries:** a message that can't be delivered is retried after 30 s,
  2 min, 10 min, 1 h and 6 h, then marked `failed`, which is recorded in
  the audit log. A 4xx answer (other than 408 or 429) fails at once,
  because a wrong URL or token won't fix itself.
- **At most 30 messages per channel per hour.** The rest are
  `suppressed`, and the next message says how many.
- **Webhook-only sources** are never reported as failing: nothing polls
  them, so Siphon can't tell.
- **Rare duplicates:** if Siphon stops between a successful send and
  recording it, the message is sent again after the restart.
- **Private addresses:** a channel on your LAN (a self-hosted ntfy) must be
  listed in `server.services.private_endpoints`, as `host:port`. Plain
  `http://` is only allowed for such a listed host.
- **`--dry-run` doesn't check the URL itself:** the URL is a secret, so the
  dry run only checks the rest. A URL that isn't allowed (plain `http://` to
  an unlisted host) is refused when you apply.
- **Email:** not built in. Use ntfy's email forwarding, or a webhook that
  sends mail.

## Troubleshooting

- **`notify test` says the url isn't reachable:** the host is private. List
  it in `server.services.private_endpoints`, or use a public URL.
- **`failed` with HTTP 401 or 403:** the token is wrong, or the topic is
  protected. Add the channel again with the right `--token`.
- **`failed` with HTTP 404:** the Slack hook was revoked, or the URL is
  wrong. Add the channel again.
- **Nothing for an approval:** check that the channel's events include
  `approval`, and that the approval started after you added the channel.


---

<!-- file: docs/tasks/schedule.md -->

# Run a task on a schedule

**Goal:** run a command, a routine or an agent at set times (every weekday
at 07:30, every Monday at 09:00, every 15 minutes) without a host timer.

## CLI

```sh
siphon new task --name standup --schedule "30 7 * * 1-5" --timezone Europe/London \
  --cmd '["curl","-fsS","-d","Standup in 30 minutes","https://ntfy.sh/your-topic"]' --yes
```

Or start from a template:

```sh
siphon template weekday-standup     # 07:30 on weekdays, a command
siphon template weekly-digest       # Mondays 09:00: fetch → local-model summary → phone
siphon template nightly-report      # every day 06:00, a routine
```

**Test without waiting** for the clock:

```sh
siphon test standup --at "2026-10-12 07:30"     # builds the event for that moment, runs nothing
siphon why standup                               # shows the next and last run
```

## Writing `at:`

| `at:` | Runs |
|---|---|
| `"30 7 * * 1-5"` | 07:30, Monday to Friday |
| `"0 9 * * 1"` | 09:00 every Monday |
| `"0 6 * * *"` | 06:00 every day |
| `"0 */4 * * *"` | every 4 hours, on the hour |
| `"0 0 1 * *"` | midnight on the 1st of each month |
| `"@daily"`, `"@hourly"`, `"@weekly"`, `"@monthly"` | the usual shortcuts |
| `"every 15m"` | every 15 minutes, from when the source started (at least 1m, including `@every …`) |

The five fields are *minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week*
(standard cron, no seconds field). Set the zone with `timezone:`; a
`TZ=`/`CRON_TZ=` prefix in `at` is refused.

## The source

```yaml
sources:
  weekly:
    type: schedule
    at: "0 9 * * 1"
    timezone: Europe/London       # IANA name; default: the host's zone
    catch_up: latest              # latest (default) | none
    data: { kind: weekly-digest } # optional, merged into the event
```

The event a rule sees:

```json
{"schedule": "0 9 * * 1", "timezone": "Europe/London", "scheduled_at": "2026-10-12T09:00:00+01:00",
 "fired_at": "2026-10-12T09:00:00.04+01:00", "catch_up": false, "kind": "weekly-digest"}
```

A rule on a schedule source defaults to `on: each` with
`id: event.scheduled_at`: each scheduled moment fires **once**, even if
Siphon restarts. `event.schedule` is the `at` expression.

**`data`:**
- It lets one schedule feed several rules
  (`when: 'event.kind == "weekly-digest"'`).
- It's plain text, stored with the event and shown in the portal, so never
  put a token in it.
- It's capped at 16 KiB.

## Missed runs

If Siphon was down at a scheduled time:

- **`catch_up: latest`** (the default) runs the **most recent** missed time
  once, when Siphon starts, with `event.catch_up: true`. Older missed
  times are skipped, and recorded in the audit (`schedule_skipped`).
- **`catch_up: none`** skips them all, and records that too. A moment
  that's less than 2 minutes late at start-up still runs; that's a
  restart, not an outage.

A new schedule never fires for times before it existed. That includes its
first moment, if Siphon was down when it came round. After a suspend or a
clock jump, Siphon notices within a minute, and handles the missed moment
by the same rule.

## Time zones and daylight saving

Times are in the source's `timezone`. Around clock changes:

- **In spring,** a time inside the skipped hour doesn't run that day.
  For example `30 1 * * *` in Europe/London on the last Sunday of March.
- **In autumn,** a schedule that runs hourly or less often runs **once** in
  the repeated hour. One that runs more often (for example `*/5 * * * *`
  or `every 10m`) keeps every real interval, so it runs through both
  passes of the hour.

If a job must run every day without exception, use `timezone: UTC`, or a
time outside 01:00–03:00.

## Agents on a schedule

Agents cost money or local compute. Siphon warns when an agent would run
more often than every 15 minutes. `limits.agent_runs_per_day`,
`cooldown` and approvals (on by default) still apply.

## Verify

- **Portal:** **Sources** shows each schedule's **next run** and last run,
  in its time zone. **Jobs** shows each run.
- **CLI:** `siphon get sources` (the NEXT column) and `siphon why <rule>`
  (schedule, next run, last run, and whether a run was missed).

## Troubleshooting

- **It didn't run at the expected time:** check `timezone` in `siphon
  why`. The default is the host's zone.
- **It ran once and never again:** the rule has an explicit `on: edge`.
  Remove it (schedule rules default to `on: each`).
- **It ran late after a restart:** that's `catch_up: latest` doing its
  job. Set `catch_up: none` if a late run is worse than no run.

<!-- file: docs/templates/alertmanager-summary.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    Summarise Prometheus alerts with a local model, then notify
# category: Ops & monitoring
# needs:    credentials/ollama-local               (siphon connect model ollama)
# secrets:  sources/alertmanager.secret            (the value must be "Bearer <token>")
# apply:    siphon apply -f alertmanager-summary.yaml --secret sources/alertmanager.secret=-
# Alertmanager:
#   receivers: [{ name: siphon, webhook_configs: [{ url: https://<siphon>/hook/alertmanager,
#     http_config: { authorization: { credentials: <token> } } }] }]
sources:
  alertmanager:
    type: webhook
    signature: token                # Alertmanager sends Authorization: Bearer <token>
    token_header: Authorization
agents:
  alert-summary:
    kind: model
    credential: ollama-local
    model: llama3.2
    prompt: |
      Alertmanager sent {{len .event.alerts}} alert(s), status {{.event.status}}, group {{.event.groupKey}}.
      Alerts: {{.event.alerts}}
      Summarise for an on-call engineer in at most three lines: what is wrong, where, how bad.
    max_turns: 2
    timeout: 5m
    approve: false                  # a read-only summary; nothing acts on it
routines:
  alert-to-phone:
    steps:
      - { id: summary, agent: alert-summary, timeout: 5m }
      - { id: notify, if: 'steps.summary.exit == 0', cmd: [curl, -fsS, -H, "Title: Alert", -d, "{{.steps.summary.output}}", https://ntfy.sh/siphon-CHANGE-ME] }
rules:
  - name: alerts-firing
    source: alertmanager
    when: 'event.status == "firing"'
    on: each
    id: event.groupKey + "/" + string(len(event.alerts))
    cooldown: 2m
    action: { routine: alert-to-phone }
```

<!-- file: docs/templates/aws-cloudwatch-alarm.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    Investigate CloudWatch alarms with an agent (EventBridge)
# category: AWS
# needs:    sources/aws-cloudwatch, sources/aws-hooks  (siphon connect aws --name aws --servers cloudwatch --webhook)
#           credentials/claude-max                     (siphon connect login claude)
# apply:    siphon apply -f aws-cloudwatch-alarm.yaml
# In EventBridge: a rule on "CloudWatch Alarm State Change" targeting the API
# destination that `siphon connect aws` printed (header X-Siphon-Key).
agents:
  alarm-investigator:
    kind: claude
    credential: claude-max
    prompt: |
      CloudWatch alarm "{{.event.detail.alarmName}}" went to ALARM in {{.event.region}}:
      {{.event.detail.state.reason}}
      Look at the alarm's history and the related log groups, then explain the likely
      cause in five lines. Read only.
    mcp: [aws-cloudwatch]
    allowed_tools: [mcp__aws-cloudwatch__get_active_alarms, mcp__aws-cloudwatch__get_alarm_history, mcp__aws-cloudwatch__describe_log_groups, mcp__aws-cloudwatch__execute_log_insights_query, mcp__aws-cloudwatch__get_logs_insight_query_results]
    max_turns: 20
    max_budget_usd: 1
    timeout: 20m                    # 55m at most with an AWS source
rules:
  - name: alarm-fired
    source: aws-hooks
    when: 'event["detail-type"] == "CloudWatch Alarm State Change" && event.detail.state.value == "ALARM"'
    on: each
    id: event.id
    cooldown: 5m
    action: { agent: alarm-investigator }
```

<!-- file: docs/templates/disk-full.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    Warn when a disk is nearly full (and again every 6 hours)
# category: Ops & monitoring
# apply:    siphon apply -f disk-full.yaml
# The URL must return JSON like {"used_pct": 93}, e.g. a node exporter
# sidecar or a tiny script behind your reverse proxy.
sources:
  disk:
    type: http
    url: https://metrics.example.com/api/disk
    poll: 5m
rules:
  - name: disk-full
    source: disk
    when: 'event.used_pct > 90'
    on: edge                        # fires on false -> true only
    repeat: 6h                      # and again every 6 h while it stays true
    action:
      cmd: [curl, -fsS, -H, "Title: Disk {{.event.used_pct}}% full", -d, "Clean up or grow the volume", https://ntfy.sh/siphon-CHANGE-ME]
```

```yaml
# title:    Diagnose a failed GitHub Actions run
# category: Code review & CI
# needs:    sources/github, sources/github-hooks   (siphon connect github --webhook; tick "Workflow runs" in GitHub)
#           credentials/claude-max                 (siphon connect login claude)
# apply:    siphon apply -f github-ci-failure.yaml
agents:
  ci-doctor:
    kind: claude
    credential: claude-max
    prompt: |
      Workflow run {{.event.workflow_run.id}} ("{{.event.workflow_run.name}}") failed on
      {{.event.workflow_run.head_branch}} in {{.event.repository.full_name}}.
      Read the failed jobs' logs and explain the most likely cause in five lines,
      with the failing step and a suggested fix. Do not re-run anything.
    mcp: [github]
    allowed_tools: [mcp__github__get_workflow_run, mcp__github__list_workflow_jobs, mcp__github__get_job_logs]
    max_turns: 20
    max_budget_usd: 1
    timeout: 15m
rules:
  - name: ci-failed
    source: github-hooks
    when: 'headers["x-github-event"] == "workflow_run" && event.action == "completed" && event.workflow_run.conclusion == "failure"'
    on: each
    id: event.workflow_run.id
    cooldown: 5m
    action: { agent: ci-doctor }
```

# title:    Suggest labels and a summary for new issues

<!-- file: docs/templates/github-pr-review.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    Review every new pull request with an agent
# category: Code review & CI
# needs:    sources/github, sources/github-hooks   (siphon connect github --webhook)
#           credentials/claude-max                 (siphon connect login claude)
# apply:    siphon apply -f github-pr-review.yaml
# The agent reads the PR through GitHub's MCP server (read-only tools) and
# reports findings in the job output. Approval is on: you decide each run.
agents:
  pr-reviewer:
    kind: claude
    credential: claude-max
    prompt: |
      Review pull request #{{.event.number}} in {{.event.repository.full_name}}
      ("{{.event.pull_request.title}}"). Read the diff, then reply with a short
      list of concrete findings (bugs, missing tests, risky changes). Never push,
      merge, comment or approve.
    mcp: [github]
    allowed_tools: [mcp__github__get_pull_request, mcp__github__get_pull_request_diff, mcp__github__get_pull_request_files]
    max_turns: 15
    max_budget_usd: 1
    timeout: 15m
rules:
  - name: review-new-prs
    source: github-hooks
    when: 'headers["x-github-event"] == "pull_request" && event.action in ["opened", "ready_for_review"] && !event.pull_request.draft'
    on: each
    id: event.pull_request.id
    cooldown: 1m
    action: { agent: pr-reviewer }
```

<!-- file: docs/templates/homeassistant-event.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    React to a Home Assistant event
# category: Homelab
# secrets:  sources/home.secret
# apply:    siphon apply -f homeassistant-event.yaml --secret sources/home.secret=-
# Home Assistant configuration.yaml:
#   rest_command:
#     siphon: { url: https://<siphon>/hook/home, method: POST, content_type: application/json,
#               headers: { X-Siphon-Key: !secret siphon_key }, payload: '{"entity":"{{ entity }}","state":"{{ state }}"}' }
# Then call rest_command.siphon from an automation.
sources:
  home:
    type: webhook
    signature: token
    token_header: X-Siphon-Key
rules:
  - name: front-door-open-at-night
    source: home
    when: 'event.entity == "binary_sensor.front_door" && event.state == "on" && now().Hour() >= 23'
    on: each
    id: event.entity + string(now().Unix() / 300)
    action:
      cmd: [curl, -fsS, -H, "Title: Front door", -d, "Opened late at night", https://ntfy.sh/siphon-CHANGE-ME]
```

<!-- file: docs/templates/mcp-build-watch.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    Watch a build status on an MCP server
# category: MCP
# apply:    siphon apply -f mcp-build-watch.yaml
sources:
  build-status:
    type: mcp
    url: https://ci.example.com/mcp
    read: { resource: "ci://builds/main" }   # exactly what is polled; nothing else is called
    poll: 2m
rules:
  - name: main-broke
    source: build-status
    when: 'event.status == "failed"'
    on: edge
    action: { cmd: [echo, "main is red: build {{.event.id}}"] }
```

<!-- file: docs/templates/mcp-task-triage.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    Triage each failed task on an MCP server with an agent
# category: MCP
# needs:    credentials/claude-max                 (siphon connect login claude)
# apply:    siphon apply -f mcp-task-triage.yaml
# One poll returns a list; for_each turns every failed task into its own fire.
sources:
  tasks:
    type: mcp
    url: https://tasks.example.com/mcp
    read: { resource: "tasks://running" }
    poll: 1m
agents:
  task-triage:
    kind: claude
    credential: claude-max
    prompt: "Task {{.item.id}} failed: {{.item.error}}. Use the task tools to read its logs and report the cause as JSON {cause, fix}."
    mcp: [tasks]
    allowed_tools: [mcp__tasks__task_get_logs, mcp__tasks__task_status]
    max_turns: 15
    max_budget_usd: 1
    timeout: 10m
rules:
  - name: task-failed
    source: tasks
    for_each: event.tasks
    id: item.id
    when: 'item.status == "failed"'
    on: each
    cooldown: 10m
    action: { agent: task-triage }
```

<!-- file: docs/templates/nightly-report.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    A nightly report on a schedule: fetch, summarise, notify
# category: Schedules
# needs:    credentials/ollama-local               (siphon connect model ollama)
# apply:    siphon apply -f nightly-report.yaml
# Runs every day at 06:00 in the given time zone; no host timer needed. If
# Siphon was down at 06:00, the missed run fires once when it starts
# (catch_up: latest).
sources:
  nightly:
    type: schedule
    at: "0 6 * * *"
    timezone: Europe/London
agents:
  reporter:
    kind: model
    credential: ollama-local
    model: llama3.2
    prompt: "Summarise these numbers for a morning report, in three lines."
    max_turns: 2
    timeout: 5m
    approve: false                  # a read-only summary; nothing acts on it
routines:
  nightly:
    steps:
      - { id: fetch, cmd: [curl, -fsS, https://metrics.example.com/api/summary], retry: { attempts: 3, base: 5s, factor: 2 } }
      - { id: summary, agent: reporter, if: 'steps.fetch.exit == 0', timeout: 5m }
      - { id: notify, if: 'steps.summary.exit == 0', cmd: [curl, -fsS, -H, "Title: Morning report", -d, "{{.steps.summary.output}}", https://ntfy.sh/siphon-CHANGE-ME] }
rules:
  - name: nightly
    source: nightly
    when: 'true'
    on: each
    id: event.scheduled_at          # one run per scheduled moment, even across restarts
    cooldown: 1h
    action: { routine: nightly }
```

<!-- file: docs/templates/service-failed.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    Get notified when a systemd service fails
# category: Ops & monitoring
# secrets:  sources/systemd.secret
# apply:    siphon apply -f service-failed.yaml --secret sources/systemd.secret=-
# On the host, an OnFailure= unit posts to Siphon (NixOS):
#   systemd.services."notify-siphon@" = { serviceConfig.Type = "oneshot"; script = ''
#     ${pkgs.curl}/bin/curl -fsS -H "X-Siphon-Key: $(cat /run/secrets/siphon-hook)" #       -d "{"unit":"$1","host":"$(hostname)"}" https://<siphon>/hook/systemd ''; scriptArgs = "%i"; };
#   systemd.services.restic-backup.unitConfig.OnFailure = "notify-siphon@%n";
sources:
  systemd:
    type: webhook
    signature: token
    token_header: X-Siphon-Key
rules:
  - name: unit-failed
    source: systemd
    when: 'event.unit != ""'
    on: each
    id: event.host + "/" + event.unit + "/" + string(int(now().Unix() / 600))   # at most one per unit per 10 min
    action:
      cmd: [curl, -fsS, -H, "Title: {{.event.unit}} failed", -d, "on {{.event.host}}", https://ntfy.sh/siphon-CHANGE-ME]
```

<!-- file: docs/templates/slack-mention-agent.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    An agent that answers when someone @mentions your Slack app
# category: Notifications & glue
# needs:    sources/slack                          (siphon connect slack)
#           credentials/ollama-local               (siphon connect model ollama)
# apply:    siphon apply -f slack-mention-agent.yaml
# Subscribe the app to the app_mention event (Event Subscriptions). The answer
# lands in the job output; posting it back needs a Slack bot token in a cmd step.
agents:
  slack-helper:
    kind: model
    credential: ollama-local
    model: llama3.2
    prompt: "Answer this message from a colleague briefly and helpfully: {{.event.event.text}}"
    max_turns: 2
    timeout: 5m
rules:
  - name: slack-mention
    source: slack
    when: 'event.type == "event_callback" && event.event.type == "app_mention"'
    on: each
    id: event.event_id
    cooldown: 10s
    action: { agent: slack-helper }
```

<!-- file: docs/templates/standard-webhooks.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    Receive Standard Webhooks (Svix, Clerk, Resend, …)
# category: Notifications & glue
# secrets:  sources/provider.secret                (the whsec_… signing secret from the provider)
# apply:    siphon apply -f standard-webhooks.yaml --secret sources/provider.secret=-
sources:
  provider:
    type: webhook
    signature: standard-webhooks    # webhook-id / webhook-timestamp / webhook-signature, 5 min window
rules:
  - name: new-signup
    source: provider
    when: 'event.type == "user.created"'
    on: each
    id: event.data.id
    action: { cmd: [echo, "new user {{.event.data.id}}"] }
```

<!-- file: docs/templates/stripe-dispute-notice.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    Get notified when a Stripe dispute is opened
# category: Notifications & glue
# needs:    sources/stripe-hooks                   (siphon connect stripe --webhook)
# apply:    siphon apply -f stripe-dispute-notice.yaml
rules:
  - name: stripe-dispute
    source: stripe-hooks
    when: 'event.type == "charge.dispute.created"'
    on: each
    id: event.id
    action:
      cmd: [curl, -fsS, -H, "Title: Stripe dispute", -d, "Dispute {{.event.data.object.id}} for {{.event.data.object.amount}} {{.event.data.object.currency}}", https://ntfy.sh/siphon-CHANGE-ME]
```

<!-- file: docs/templates/summarise-webhook.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    Summarise any incoming payload with a local model
# category: Local LLM
# needs:    credentials/ollama-local               (siphon connect model ollama)
# secrets:  sources/digest.secret
# apply:    siphon apply -f summarise-webhook.yaml --secret sources/digest.secret=-
sources:
  digest:
    type: webhook
    signature: token
    token_header: X-Siphon-Key
agents:
  digest-agent:
    kind: model
    credential: ollama-local
    model: llama3.2
    prompt: "Summarise this for a status update, in three bullet points: {{.event}}"
    max_turns: 2
    timeout: 5m
rules:
  - name: digest
    source: digest
    when: 'true'
    on: each
    id: string(event)
    cooldown: 30s
    action: { agent: digest-agent }
```

<!-- file: docs/templates/upstream-status.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    Know when a provider you depend on has an incident
# category: Ops & monitoring
# apply:    siphon apply -f upstream-status.yaml
# Any Atlassian Statuspage works the same way (GitHub, Cloudflare, OpenAI, …):
# swap the URL. indicator is none | minor | major | critical.
sources:
  github-status:
    type: http
    url: https://www.githubstatus.com/api/v2/status.json
    poll: 2m
rules:
  - name: github-degraded
    source: github-status
    when: 'event.status.indicator != "none"'
    on: edge
    action:
      cmd: [curl, -fsS, -H, "Title: GitHub incident", -d, "{{.event.status.description}}", https://ntfy.sh/siphon-CHANGE-ME]
```

<!-- file: docs/templates/uptime-kuma-down.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    Push a notification when an Uptime Kuma monitor goes down
# category: Ops & monitoring
# needs:    sources/uptime-kuma                    (siphon connect uptime-kuma)
# apply:    siphon apply -f uptime-kuma-down.yaml
rules:
  - name: monitor-down
    source: uptime-kuma
    when: 'event.heartbeat != nil && event.heartbeat.status == 0'
    on: each
    id: string(event.monitor.id) + "/" + event.heartbeat.time
    action:
      cmd: [curl, -fsS, -H, "Title: {{.event.monitor.name}} is down", -d, "{{.event.msg}}", https://ntfy.sh/siphon-CHANGE-ME]
```

<!-- file: docs/templates/webhook-command.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    Run a command when a signed webhook arrives
# category: Notifications & glue
# secrets:  sources/deploy-hook.secret
# apply:    siphon apply -f webhook-command.yaml --secret sources/deploy-hook.secret=-
# The sender signs the body with HMAC-SHA256 (hex) in X-Signature and POSTs
# to https://<siphon>/hook/deploy-hook.
sources:
  deploy-hook:
    type: webhook
    signature: sha256
    signature_header: X-Signature
rules:
  - name: deploy-done
    source: deploy-hook
    when: 'event.status == "success"'
    on: each
    id: event.id
    action: { cmd: [echo, "deploy {{.event.id}} finished"] }   # argv, never a shell
```


---

<!-- file: docs/templates/webhook-to-ntfy.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    Forward any webhook to your phone
# category: Notifications & glue
# secrets:  sources/inbox.secret
# apply:    siphon apply -f webhook-to-ntfy.yaml --secret sources/inbox.secret=-
# Anything that can POST JSON with a header (scripts, cron, IFTTT, n8n):
#   curl -H "X-Siphon-Key: <secret>" -d '{"title":"Hi","message":"It works"}' https://<siphon>/hook/inbox
sources:
  inbox:
    type: webhook
    signature: token
    token_header: X-Siphon-Key
rules:
  - name: forward
    source: inbox
    when: 'event.message != ""'
    on: each
    id: event.title + event.message
    action:
      cmd: [curl, -fsS, -H, "Title: {{.event.title}}", -d, "{{.event.message}}", https://ntfy.sh/siphon-CHANGE-ME]
```

<!-- file: docs/templates/weekday-standup.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    A weekday reminder on a schedule (07:30, Monday to Friday)
# category: Schedules
# apply:    siphon apply -f weekday-standup.yaml
# The simplest schedule: a command at set times. Swap the action for an
# agent or a routine once it works. Test it without waiting:
#   siphon test standup-reminder --at "2026-10-12 07:30"
sources:
  weekdays:
    type: schedule
    at: "30 7 * * 1-5"
    timezone: Europe/London
rules:
  - name: standup-reminder
    source: weekdays
    when: 'true'
    on: each
    id: event.scheduled_at
    action:
      cmd: [curl, -fsS, -H, "Title: Standup in 30 minutes", -d, "Notes: https://wiki.example.com/standup", https://ntfy.sh/siphon-CHANGE-ME]
```

<!-- file: docs/templates/weekly-digest.yaml -->

```yaml
# title:    A weekly digest on a schedule: every Monday at 09:00
# category: Schedules
# needs:    credentials/ollama-local               (siphon connect model ollama)
# apply:    siphon apply -f weekly-digest.yaml
# The URL should return JSON for last week (for example a metrics or
# ticket-count endpoint). The summary is pushed to your phone with ntfy.
sources:
  weekly:
    type: schedule
    at: "0 9 * * 1"
    timezone: Europe/London
    data: { kind: weekly-digest }
agents:
  digest-writer:
    kind: model
    credential: ollama-local
    model: llama3.2
    prompt: "Write a five-bullet weekly digest from this data. Lead with what changed."
    max_turns: 2
    timeout: 5m
    approve: false                  # a read-only summary
routines:
  weekly-digest:
    steps:
      - { id: fetch, cmd: [curl, -fsS, https://metrics.example.com/api/last-week], retry: { attempts: 3, base: 10s, factor: 2 } }
      - { id: digest, agent: digest-writer, if: 'steps.fetch.exit == 0', timeout: 5m }
      - { id: notify, if: 'steps.digest.exit == 0', cmd: [curl, -fsS, -H, "Title: Weekly digest", -d, "{{.steps.digest.output}}", https://ntfy.sh/siphon-CHANGE-ME] }
rules:
  - name: weekly-digest
    source: weekly
    when: 'event.kind == "weekly-digest"'
    on: each
    id: event.scheduled_at
    cooldown: 1h
    action: { routine: weekly-digest }
```
